title: Import and replacement
summary: Hosted Import offers a backup first and asks for explicit consent to replace the destination. A hosted import deletes all of the destination's stored files, including QA artifacts, and keeps only the files in the archive. It fetches an allowlisted signed link server-to-server, verifies the archive and restores artifacts before serving. Success completes the replacement and removes the prior database; fresh machine connections and unrelated organization creation work immediately. After publication, importing the saved backup is the only way to restore the previous destination. Only an import actually in flight fences its target organization. Recovery before publication restores the original automatically; recovery after publication finishes cleanup and never restores the original. Local and self-host move exports pause writers, drain clients except autovacuum, and prove an exclusive TEMPLATE copy with source admission kept closed to stamp zero_writable_app_sessions=True. Ordinary backups stamp False and cannot enter hosted replacement. Resume restores the source explicitly; archive credentials do not copy working machine access. Hosted replacement establishes the verified importing person as a destination owner while preserving restored owners and other members' roles. Local import binds the oldest active human only when that person already holds org owner; normal role changes and invitations retain active-owner protection.
